results.title: 8BitDo Arcade Controller Pro Puts Fighting-Game Controls and Customization at Your Fingertips
results.content:
The Pro looks most relevant to fighting-game players who already want a leverless controller and expect to use its customization features. Five programmable buttons, on-device settings, hot-swappable switches, and wired or wireless connectivity give them several ways to tailor the setup.

It’s a less obvious choice for someone who is already comfortable with a conventional gamepad or arcade stick and rarely changes controller settings. An all-button directional layout is a different control method, and a screen or extra programmable buttons won’t automatically improve anyone’s results. [...] Players already familiar with leverless controllers should recognize the appeal of the layout. For longtime joystick users, however, switching to individual directional buttons means learning a different way to enter movement commands. The Pro offers another approach to fighting-game controls, not a guaranteed shortcut to better results.

## Settings on the built-in screen

The 1.47-inch display does more than show inputs and battery status. With built-in Ultimate Software, it also provides access to essential settings without requiring a computer for every adjustment.

The controller supports 8BitDo Ultimate Software V2 for additional configuration, giving players both on-device controls and a desktop software option. [...] Price:  TBD Where to Pre-order: 8BitDo

The 8BitDo Arcade Controller Pro takes that all-button approach and adds mechanical switches, five programmable controls, wireless connectivity, and a built-in display. Designed for Windows, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2, it puts a range of configuration options directly on the controller.

For players who like to fine-tune their setup, the screen is the most interesting addition. But the Pro also includes practical touches such as a removable magnetic wrist rest, hot-swappable switches, and a quick-release faceplate.

results.title: First impressions: 8BitDo's Arcade Controller Pro
results.content:
5 min read

0 comments

Image Credit: 8BitDo

8BitDo chose Evo 2026, the world’s longest-running fighting game tournament, to unveil the Arcade Controller Pro, and that tells you everything about who they made it for.

The all-button design drops the joystick altogether, packing every input into a tight grid built for fighting games. I’ve watched the leverless format grow from a niche modder obsession into a tournament standard, and a major brand committing to a polished version feels overdue. The launch window matters too, with pre-orders opening in September after the Las Vegas show wraps.

## A layout tuned for tight inputs

First impressions: 8BitDo's Arcade Controller Pro is a leverless fight stick done right

Image Credit: 8BitDo [...] ## Customization you can do mid-event

Hot-swappable switches turn a fight stick from a fixed tool into something you tune to your own feel, and 8BitDo went with its Core Green low-profile linear switches co-developed with Kailh. Three spare switches and a puller live inside the controller, so a dead switch never benches you in the middle of a bracket run when swapping it out matters most.

The quick-release tempered glass faceplate pops up with a button on the back, giving you quick access to the internals. Five lock caps stored in the wrist rest let you block any of the P1 through P5 buttons to prevent accidental presses, a smart touch for players who keep brushing a key they never meant to hit.

## Connection options without compromise [...] EVO Championship Series

Image Credit: Evo

My biggest gripe comes down to the compatibility list, because the Arcade Controller Pro covers Switch, Switch 2, and Windows while leaving PlayStation off. Debuting a tournament-flavored fight stick at Evo and skipping the platform that hosts so many marquee brackets is a strange call. Evo runs flagship titles on PlayStation 5 hardware, and the official ruleset spells out PS5-specific controller exemptions, so the omission cuts off players who want a single stick for their main event.

results.title: 8BitDo Launches The Arcade Controller Pro For Hardcore Fighting Game Fans
results.content:
Like its predecessor, the Arcade Controller Pro is a rectangular pad that to the uninitiated looks more like something you might use to make electronic music than play fighting games. But those buttons are used to control everything from your inputs to your movement, and 8BitDo has made them smaller, with tighter spacing between them, to make the whole controller easier to access.

The original Arcade Controller featured four programmable buttons, and the Pro adds a fifth to the far left of the pad. 8BitDo says this gives you even more control options while leaving more room for your left hand to move naturally. Also new is a built-in display that shows you your inputs and battery status, while letting you make quick settings adjustments. [...] The Arcade Controller Pro features hot-swappable switches and redesigned round button caps that you can install from any angle. You can also swap out the programmable P1-P5 button caps with flat lock caps (five are included) for even more insurance against jabbing a button you didn't mean to in the heat of a fight. The various customization options are designed to give you the perfect setup for how you like to play, and you can go even deeper with 8BitDo's Ultimate Software V2, which lets you customize button mapping and create macros. [...] # 8BitDo launches the Arcade Controller Pro for hardcore fighting game fans

It’s the second leverless controller the company has released.

Last year, 8BitDo shipped its first leverless arcade controller for all the joystick-shunning fighting game enthusiasts, and also the more casual players who might be interested in trying the all-button approach. Be under no illusion about who the new Arcade Controller Pro is for: serious fighters, in 8BitDo's own words.

results.title: 8BitDo Arcade Controller Pro Preview - Preview - Nintendo World Report
results.content:
If you were already familiar with the 8BitDo Arcade Controller, I can’t say that the Arcade Controller Pro is reinventing the wheel here. That said, the tweaks and changes presented here are very promising. The lightweight design and ease of use that is expected from 8BitDo is still one of the reasons why I really liked using my Arcade Controller. For the pros you are trading in the weight of a hitbox for the flexibility of a leverless controller. But the Pro seems to be fixing some of the key complaints that held it back from reigning supreme. Time will tell how many fights it can last, but for a first impression this seems to be a killer combo.
